subject: GoalStream evaluation — goals on a page and acceptance signals
messages:
From: Sylvia Park <sylvia@goalstream.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@goalstream.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: GoalStream evaluation — goals on a page and acceptance signals

Hi Karthik / Lauren,

Thanks again for the product overview yesterday. We want to move from demo -> scoped evaluation next week. To speed procurement and to set internal expectations, can you share a one-page "goals on a page" for the MAP that defines:

- Primary success criteria (what does “pass” look like for the evaluation?)
- Exit gates (conditions that must be met before we commit to pilot)
- Minimal acceptance tests we can run in our environment (smoke tests)
- Timeline and owner for each workstream (integration, security, ops)

I've attached our RFP context and a short list of internal priorities. Procurement (cc'd) will need clear acceptance tests for their checklist.

High level constraints: production-like traffic is not required for this eval; we need reproducible results on a subset of our data, and clear definitions for latency and inference accuracy tolerances.

Can you get a draft MAP by EOD Wednesday? We'll consolidate and circle back with any clarifying Qs.

Best,

Sylvia Park
VP, Product Operations
GoalStream

Attachment: GoalStream-RFP-Context.pdf
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sylvia Park <sylvia@goalstream.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 12:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: GoalStream evaluation — goals on a page and acceptance signals

Sylvia — thanks, understood. Drafting the one-pager and attaching our MAP template (Redwood-MAP-template.xlsx) so you can see the fields we'll fill. Quick outline below; the attached contains the scoring rubric and an initial set of acceptance tests.

Draft goals (topline):
- Functional: Generate contextual recommendations with >= 85% relevance against labelled sample set (80% pass, 90% stretch)
- Latency: 95th percentile request latency <= 220ms at a per-user qps of 0.5 (measured in dedicated test harness)
- Reliability: <= 1% error rate for 7-day smoke window
- Security/compliance: No user data persisted outside customer VPC during test, KMS integration verified

Proposed exit gates (examples):
1) Integration complete: SDK + network config validated and internal smoke tests run (owner: GoalStream eng)
2) Quality threshold met: Sample accuracy >= pass threshold on labelled set (owner: GoalStream PM)
3) Performance baseline: Measured latency below threshold on representative runs (owner: Redwood SRE)
4) Security checklist: Audit log + KMS proof-of-evidence (owner: GoalStream SecOps)

Suggested minimal acceptance tests (smoke):
- End-to-end request with 10 labelled queries -> verify response shape + confidence scoring
- Latency run: 1k sequential requests to measure p95 on replica infra
- Failover: Simulate a degraded CUDA node and confirm automatic fallback to secondary pool
- Data handling: Verify request payloads are transient and not logged to external storage

Timeline (high level):
- Day 0 (kickoff): Share test accounts and stub data
- Day 2-3: Integration + network verification
- Day 4-7: Run acceptance tests, collect artifacts
- Day 8: Review and decision (go/no-go)

Will attach the filled template by Wednesday EOD. If you want different thresholds, call them out and we'll adjust.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood-MAP-template.xlsx
From: Sylvia Park <sylvia@goalstream.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@goalstream.com>, procurement@goalstream.com
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: GoalStream evaluation — goals on a page and acceptance signals

Thanks Karthik — this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Accuracy: our labelled set has some edge cases (abbreviations, mixed language). Can you add a concordance/case-slice test so we can see per-slice pass rates?
- Latency: the 220ms p95 is acceptable as-is but we need p50 and p95 buckets by region (we're in US-only for this eval).
- Timeline: procurement needs explicit artifact names they can reference in the contract (logs, evidence of KMS key exchange, signed test report).

Procurement note: procurement@goalstream.com — we'll expect a simple attestation doc from Redwood that includes: list of acceptance test runs, timestamps, artifact links, and a short remediation plan if a test fails.

We'll review your filled template once you share it. Also looping Daniel (engineering lead) for the concordance slices and to align owners.

Best,
Sylvia

Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 11:20:00 -0800
Subject: Internal — standardize acceptance artifacts for GoalStream

Karthik / Monica,

Good thread. Quick guidance from me before we finalize the MAP: please make the acceptance artifacts discrete and machine-verifiable where possible. Procurement will want traceable evidence they can attach to contract clauses. Suggested minimal artifact list (one-liners to include in the MAP):

- Test report (PDF) with run IDs, timestamps, and pass/fail per test case
- Raw perf traces (compressed) + p50/p95/p99 summary CSV
- Sample request/response pairs (n=50) with labels and concordance scoring per slice
- Security attestation: KMS exchange log + audit-log snippet showing request/handshake

Also define exact owners and escalation path if a test fails (who owns remediation and SLA to re-run test).

Finally, set a clear go/no-go decision meeting: Day 9 review with GoalStream PM + Redwood PM + SRE. Put a hard freeze on changes 24 hours before the decision window.

Thanks — keep it concise; I'll review the draft and sign off.

Lauren Bishop
Director, Customer Success, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sylvia Park <sylvia@goalstream.com>, Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@goalstream.com>, procurement@goalstream.com
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Final MAP excerpt + acceptance smoke cases — GoalStream (DEAL-7832)

Sylvia / Daniel / procurement team,

Thanks for the feedback — attached is the filled MAP excerpt and a short markdown that enumerates the smoke cases (acceptance-smoke-cases.md). Summary of agreed items (TL;DR):

Primary success criteria:
- Concordance: overall >= 85% on labelled set, with per-slice threshold: abbreviations >= 75%, mixed-language >= 70%
- Latency: p50 <= 110ms, p95 <= 220ms in US region (test harness: redwood-eval-01)
- Reliability: error rate <= 1% across acceptance runs

Exit gates (all required):
1) Integration validated: SDK + network (evidence: integration-run-<id>.log)
2) Concordance threshold met on labelled set (artifact: concordance-report-<id>.csv)
3) Performance baseline achieved (artifact: perf-summary-<id>.csv)
4) Security checklist completed (artifact: kms-exchange-<id>.txt + attestation.pdf)

Acceptance tests (minimal):
- Slice concordance: run 500 labelled queries over slices -> output concordance-report-<id>.csv (pass rules above)
- Latency sweep: 1k requests at qps=0.5 -> perf-summary-<id>.csv (p50/p95 metrics)
- Failover test: shut down a node in dedicated pool and verify fallback within 30s -> failover-log-<id>.txt
- Data handling check: sample payloads demonstrate no persistent logs beyond allocated ephemeral storage -> data-handling-evidence-<id>.txt

Artifacts we will deliver (names to use in contract):
- concordance-report-<id>.csv, perf-summary-<id>.csv, integration-run-<id>.log, kms-exchange-<id>.txt, acceptance-report-<id>.pdf

Timeline (agreed):
- Day 0 (Thu Nov 12): kickoff + credentials exchange
- Day 1-2: integration + network config
- Day 3-6: run acceptance tests and collect artifacts
- Day 7 (Wed Nov 18): internal review + remediation window (if any)
- Day 8 (Thu Nov 19): formal decision meeting -> go/no-go

Next steps:
1) Procurement: confirm that the artifact names above map to the clauses you need.
2) Daniel: please share the labelled sample set (or a secure s3 pointer) and define the concordance slices.
3) We will start kickoff tomorrow morning if you confirm credentials.

Attaching: Redwood-MAP-template.xlsx (filled), acceptance-smoke-cases.md, and a short one-page acceptance-report template (acceptance-report-template.pdf).

If that looks good I will upload artifact generation hooks to the shared drive so procurement can reference the links in the contract.

Regards,

Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood-MAP-template.xlsx, acceptance-smoke-cases.md, acceptance-report-template.pdf
